affectedPublicSurfaces: STOP REASONS ON THE RUN LIST — a seller- and operator-visible surface. #1707 already added `no_diagnosis_codes`, `price_lever_locked`, `scope_unavailable` and `declined` to the `StopReason` enum, the DB CHECK and the TS union; this slice makes Optimize Product ACTUALLY REACH all four. Each ends the run `completed` (never `failed`) with its own cause, so the four facts are distinguishable in the run list and countable in run quality. Today's shipped enum (`services/agent/status.py`) carries `final_response`, `confirmation_declined`, `concluded_without_changes`, `tool_error_unrecoverable` and eleven more — the four causes are the discriminators ADR-090 d.7 puts beside `concluded_without_changes`, not replacements for it.

THE COMPLETION MESSAGE — four DISTINCT Vietnamese seller messages, one per cause, each through the ADR-070 outbound banned-pattern guard. One generic 'nothing to do' would make four different facts indistinguishable, which is exactly the failure ADR-088 diagnosed on `final_response`. The cause NAMES are internal identifiers and must never appear in the seller's words (S-NFR-4).

IMPACT READINGS GAIN ROWS FOR DISCOUNT WRITES — the measure. `classify_mutation_kinds` (`backend/src/juli_backend/workers/impact_reader/classify.py:57-66`) keys off `price_update`/`image_uri`/`title`/`description` and returns `[]` for a discount payload, so a discount execution is SELECTED as due by `measurable_tool_names()` (because #1778's tool is WRITE-registered) and then SILENTLY SKIPPED. This slice adds a DISCOUNT MUTATION KIND to `MutationKind` (`services/impact/metric_map.py:52-66`, today `SEO_KEYWORDS_TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION`/`IMAGE`/`PRICE`) with its metric spec, plus the classify branch that recognises a discount payload. A discount is a PRICE-SHAPED mutation, so it reads the EXISTING revenue metric (`GMV` in `metric_map.py`) — CTOR IS NOT A METRIC ANYWHERE IN THIS CODEBASE (`METRIC_MAP` holds impressions, ctr, conversion_rate, items_sold, gmv, sku_orders, gmv_per_order and nothing else) and is NOT introduced here.

THE LISTING-EDIT CLASSIFICATION IS A GOLDEN. A listing edit must classify EXACTLY as it does today, byte-for-byte — adding a branch to a heuristic that already keys off four payload fields is the classic place to change an existing verdict by accident.
READINGS STAY HEDGED at 7 and 14 days on the EXISTING windows (`services/impact/windows.py`). No new window, no new confidence vocabulary, no new hedging rule.

REPEAT-CONSENT ELIGIBILITY refuses this workflow key. ADR-090 d.6 NARROWS ADR-055 d.19, which listed `optimize_product_2` as Repeat-consent *Eligible* — that eligibility was assessed against a listing-content edit, and the lever is now a priced, expiring promotion. Every run needs a fresh approval AND a fresh confirmation. The eligibility check is the enforcement point, not the prompt.

SILENT LAPSE. The 30-day discount expires on its own and V1 DOES NOTHING: no renewal, no scheduled re-card, no revert. A successor card comes ONLY from the standard nightly ADR-087 emission path, where the partial unique index (one active card per shop/workflow/subject) makes a duplicate STRUCTURALLY impossible rather than merely unlikely. This v1 behaviour deliberately TRIMS ADR-090 d.6's lapse-driven revision — the spec records the trim, and the emission path is identical either way, so nothing is built twice.

A RUN THAT WROTE NOTHING PRODUCES NO IMPACT READING and counts SEPARATELY from a failure (S-FR-7, `CONTEXT.md`'s four-metric separation). The absence of a row is the assertion, not the presence of a zero.
A VENDOR ERROR ON THE DIAGNOSIS READ that survives retry STAYS on the failure terminal (`tool_error_unrecoverable`, status `failed`). It must never be laundered into one of the four honest causes.

NO HTTP route contract changes and NO schema change: #1707 already extended the enum, the DB CHECK and the TS union, and the new mutation kind is a CODE-LEVEL enum value in `services/impact/metric_map.py`, never a database object. Nothing under `apps/`, `packages/` or `ios/` is touched — this epic's doNotLoad list.

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: Pre-merge: pytest driven by the REAL `WorkflowRunner` against the fake LLM adapter (built on `LLMService.complete`'s real signature) from the worktree root with `PYTHONPATH` pinned to that worktree's own `backend/src`, against a REAL Postgres 16 migrated to head — never SQLite, because the run rows, the `impact_readings` unique key on `(tool_execution_id, metric, kind)` and the ABSENCE assertions the journey depends on are Postgres behaviour. EACH OF THE FOUR CAUSES IS REACHED THROUGH A REAL RUN, never by writing a stop reason into a row by hand, and THE READER IS EXERCISED AGAINST REAL `tool_executions` ROWS written by #1778's persistence path rather than hand-built payloads. Post-deploy: the candidate's `/health` plus ONE authenticated read of an existing COMPLETED run whose stop reason and impact readings must be unchanged. No public traffic reaches a candidate task set and no vendor write occurs.
candidateVerificationJourney.notes: apiSideEffectsInScope is FALSE: this slice adds no vendor call at all — it names end states and classifies payloads that already exist. workersDisabledOnCandidate is FALSE because both halves of the slice live in workers: `WorkflowRunner` reaches the end states inside the Celery worker and the impact reader IS a Celery beat task. A candidate with workers disabled could exercise neither, and the journey would prove nothing.

migrationCompatibility.notes: NO SCHEMA CHANGE. No column, index, constraint, table or grant is touched and NO Alembic revision file is created — the executor must not open `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`. #1707 ALREADY extended the `stop_reason` enum, the DB CHECK and the TS union, so the four causes are existing permitted values that this slice merely makes reachable; the discount MUTATION KIND is a CODE-LEVEL Python enum value in `services/impact/metric_map.py` and is stored in `impact_readings.kind` as an ordinary string, never as a database enum type or a CHECK member. Verify that claim against #1707's landed migration before writing a line — if the CHECK does not in fact permit all four causes, STOP and report rather than adding a migration under this issue. Stable and candidate run the identical schema: a stable process reading a run whose stop reason is one of the four resolves it because #1707's enum already contains it, and a stable impact reader that meets a row with the new mutation kind must ignore it rather than crash — assert that tolerance pre-merge.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Nothing about the deployed system changes: the four causes stay unreachable vocabulary that #1707 shipped but nothing produces, a discount write keeps classifying as `[]` and being silently skipped by the impact reader, repeat-consent eligibility keeps whatever ADR-055 d.19 left it as, and a lapse keeps doing nothing. Nothing is exposed, nothing is partially applied, no vendor call is made, no data hazard.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Code-only rollback: redeploy the previous release and restart `juli-api` AND `juli-celery-worker` together. There is no schema to revert and no downgrade to run — this slice owns no migration. ROWS WRITTEN WITH THE NEW MUTATION KIND STAY READABLE: `impact_readings.kind` holds a string, so the reverted reader meets a value it does not recognise and must IGNORE it rather than crash — assert that tolerance pre-merge, because it is the whole reason the revert is safe. THE FOUR CAUSES REMAIN VALID VALUES in the enum, the DB CHECK and the TS union that #1707 shipped, so a run completed under the candidate with `price_lever_locked` still loads, still renders and still counts after the revert; what is lost is the ability to REACH those causes on new runs, not the ability to read old ones. State the direction of the risk plainly: after a revert, a discount write stops being measured again, and repeat consent is no longer refused at the eligibility check — the revert is safe for data and re-opens a policy gap. A run SUSPENDED at CONFIRM across the rollback resumes correctly: consent is bound by `params_sha` over the tool call's arguments and neither the arguments nor the hash function move in this slice.

doNotInfer: Do NOT write a BASE PRICE, and do NOT let an end state be reached by taking one. `resources.products.update_prices` has no caller on this path (#1773); `price_lever_locked` is what happens INSTEAD of a base-price fallback, and ADR-090 d.1 rejected that fallback by name.
The MODEL NEVER PICKS A DEPTH. This slice adds no numeric parameter; if one appears, the work has drifted into #1778's pricing rule.
Do NOT ship a DEFAULT SHOP MAXIMUM or any default depth, in code, config, fixture or test data. #1775's setting is required and seller-confirmed.

Do NOT CLAIM A TIKTOK TIER OR A CODE THE API DID NOT RETURN (OP-NFR-2). The `no_diagnosis_codes` message says Juli found nothing to act on — it must not imply TikTok graded the listing. The Price Diagnostics tier and the 14 card recommendations are never claimed.

Do NOT reach for SEARCH ACTIVITIES to detect a lapse. `POST /promotion/202309/activities/search` does not exist as a usable read (contract-collection A-25; `endpoints.md:509`). V1 does NOTHING on lapse; there is no polling loop to write.

Do NOT enable REPEAT CONSENT. It is BARRED for this workflow key in v1 (ADR-090 d.6, narrowing ADR-055 d.19's `optimize_product_2` eligibility). Refuse it at the ELIGIBILITY CHECK, never only in prompt text, and do not delete the repeat-consent component — dark-flagging this workflow key is the change.

Do NOT READ A MIGRATION NUMBER FROM HEAD — do not write a migration at all. This slice has no schema change; #1707 already landed the enum, the CHECK and the TS union. Never run `alembic heads`, never read the tip of `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`, never derive a number from the newest filename. Migration numbers are RESERVED BY META. If the CHECK turns out not to permit a cause, STOP and report rather than adding one here.

DO NOT INTRODUCE CTOR. It exists nowhere in this codebase — `METRIC_MAP` holds impressions, ctr, conversion_rate, items_sold, gmv, sku_orders and gmv_per_order — and the spec's OP-NFR-3 wording naming CTOR is a recorded spec-vs-code conflict where the code is right. A CTOR MetricSpec and its backing daily column are v2 if wanted.

Do NOT change how a LISTING EDIT classifies. The existing four branches and their deterministic order are a golden; a discount branch that reorders, absorbs or shadows an existing verdict silently re-attributes historical impact.
Do NOT shape a discount payload so the existing `price_update` branch classifies it. A faked classification is worse than a skipped execution — add the kind honestly.

Do NOT build LAPSE-DRIVEN CARD REVISIONS, a renewal, a revert, or a scheduled re-card. V1 is SILENT LAPSE (spec §2 Deferred, trimming ADR-090 d.6); a successor card comes only from the standard nightly emission path.
Do NOT emit a card outside the STANDARD PATH. ADR-087 decision 2's partial unique index is what makes a duplicate structurally impossible; a bespoke emission bypasses the one guarantee that holds.
Do NOT turn a NO-CHANGE run into a failure, and do NOT write a zero-valued impact reading for it. Absence of a row is the correct record (S-FR-7).

Do NOT map a VENDOR ERROR onto an honest cause. A diagnosis-read error surviving retry stays on the failure terminal; conflating the two hides a broken integration behind an honest-looking completion.

Do NOT put an internal identifier in seller-facing text. `no_diagnosis_codes`, `price_lever_locked`, `scope_unavailable` and `declined` are stop-reason names; the seller reads Vietnamese, second person, through the outbound guard, with no projected impact magnitude and no causal claim (S-NFR-4).
Do NOT touch `apps/**`, `ios/**`, `packages/**`, `docs/product/design/**` or the TikTok corpora catalogs (ADR-051) — this epic's doNotLoad list.

Bind every test collaborator to the REAL object's signature — real `tool_executions` rows from #1778's path, the real classifier, the real `WorkflowRunner`, the real eligibility check, the existing fake LLM adapter over `LLMService.complete`. A `**kwargs` double proves routing, never that the real call would work.
